title: Constrain autonomous USB-C PD sinks to an explicitly protected supported profile
problem: A generic PD-sink request can silently become an unsafe high-power board with unverified switches, magnetics, thermal assumptions, or supplier claims.
rootCause: Negotiated input power was not coupled to a fixed PDO, normally-off power path, protection ratings, conversion limits, and live-sourcing evidence.
solution: Use the Board004 9V/2A maximum sink contract with 5V/1.5A fallback, STUSB4500 control, a 30V PMOS, 24V TVS, fuse, 32V-rated 5V/2A buck, rated magnetics/capacitors, a connector-notch outline, and a fail-closed dual-provider gate.
limitations: Live evidence expires and must be refreshed at generation time.
PDO NVM programming and thermal validation remain manufacturing gates.
